clue.text: Flirt I catch in embrace of that woman behind piano

indicators.note: behind places the later pieces after the piano letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: in embrace of means the pronoun's letters hug the others

parts.note: that woman is the pronoun her
to catch a fish is to land it

explanation.surface: A man confesses he has been caught flirting, held in the arms of a woman sitting behind the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs for dallying lightly with someone romantically, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Slight reaction as card game is incomplete

indicators.note: is incomplete says the game's name loses its final letter

parts.note: piquet is an old two-handed card game

explanation.surface: Someone shows a little irritation because the card game was left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment at being slighted is the sense, a reaction to an affront or snub.

clue.text: I haven't suggested he was formidable

indicators.note: suggested hints that the letters of haven't only point to, rather than spell, the words wanted, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
terrible in its old sense means awe-inspiring, formidable

explanation.surface: Someone denies having claimed that a man was formidable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suggested' is the anagram signal for the letters of haven't. The Russian epithet Grozny really means formidable or awe-inspiring rather than wicked, so the whole statement is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to a person: the sixteenth-century Russian tsar Ivan IV, whose nickname is this phrase.

clue.text: Last, in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming last means coming behind every other one
a phrase meaning nevertheless, when all is said and done

explanation.surface: Two phrases set side by side like a thesaurus entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means behind all others, and idiomatically means nevertheless or despite what was expected.

clue.text: Jo's bottle?

parts.note: Jo is half of the name John; demi means half, so a half-John's bottle is this big wicker-covered vessel

explanation.surface: A question about a bottle belonging to someone called Jo.
explanation.walkthrough: Jo is the first half of John, and DEMI is the prefix meaning half, so Jo is a 'demi-John'.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large narrow-necked bottle, often wicker-cased, used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: Spike resistance with returning tennis player's challenge?

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
a player waiting to return serve might dare the server with the words ace me

explanation.surface: A tennis player rises to a challenge on return of serve, perhaps spiking the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike is botanical here: a raceme is a flower spike with stalked flowers along a central stem.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany this is a flower cluster arranged along an unbranched axis, a kind of flower spike.

clue.text: Character number eleven involved in last stand-he's well padded up for a quick run

definitions.text: he's well padded up for a quick run

indicators.note: involved in means the letter is wrapped inside the stand

parts.note: a bier is the stand a coffin rests on, the last stand anyone takes
K is the eleventh letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: the number eleven batsman in the last-wicket stand, padded up and ready to run.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where number eleven bats last and wears leg pads, but the padding belongs to a leather-clad motorcyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist wears protective padded leathers for fast rides, so the cryptic description fits the rider.

clue.text: Make cards illegal, say — the ruin of the Irish

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to ban jacks is to outlaw those cards, the knaves

explanation.surface: Banning certain playing cards proves the downfall of the Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish slang verb means to wreck or break something, so it is ruin as the Irish say it.

clue.text: Joint followed by cold food that's painful in the mouth

indicators.note: followed by puts the food after the joint

parts.note: a knuckle is a finger joint
a sandwich is typically a cold snack

explanation.surface: A menu note: a cut of meat followed by a cold dish that hurts to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint and food lure you to a menu, and knuckle can be meat too; the phrase is slang for a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a punch in the face, which is certainly painful when it lands on the mouth.

clue.text: Given decree nisi, almost had to move house

indicators.note: to move tells us the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost signals that the last letter of nisi is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: After getting the provisional divorce order, someone almost had to move out of the marital home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts NISI to NIS; 'to move' shuffles DECREE plus NIS. A decree nisi was the English provisional divorce order.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling, the place where one lives, a synonym for house.

clue.text: As not empty, I'm not sure 'it's the minimum amount

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: not empty means emptied, keeping just the outer letters of not

parts.note: um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: A hesitant speaker guessing at how small a share is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not empty' reads as 'not' emptied, so only its outer letters N and T survive.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a quantum is the smallest discrete amount of a quantity such as energy.

clue.text: Learn to swear? Knock it on the head!

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
to cuss is to swear

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to stop learning bad language: knock it on the head!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock it on the head' looks like the idiom for stop it, but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To concuss someone is to injure the brain with a blow, literally knocking them on the head.

clue.text: Answer to one knocking perhaps ——a key

definitions.meaning: what you might call out to a visitor at the door: come in
the keyboard key that confirms a command

explanation.surface: Wondering how to respond to someone knocking, a key in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Called to a visitor it means come in; on a keyboard it names the return key.

clue.text: Fix verbal agreement? Get stuffed!

parts.note: a fix is a jam, a predicament

indicators.note: verbal signals that the agreement word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: Someone asked to settle a spoken deal tells the other party rudely to get stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal agreement' looks like a spoken contract, but 'verbal' means said aloud: PACT spoken is PACKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Crammed full to bursting, so completely filled is the shared sense.

clue.text: Furtive-take your word for it?

parts.note: to steal is to take
thy is the old word for your

explanation.surface: A shifty person asks whether to accept someone's promise at face value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take your word for it' is the idiom for believing someone; here it splits into take and an archaic word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe sly, secretive behaviour intended to avoid notice, a straight synonym.

clue.text: An essential for car? For Ferrari, yes please

parts.note: si is Italian for yes, the language of Ferrari
to delight is to please

explanation.surface: An Italian carmaker accepting an offer of an essential car part.
explanation.definitionFit: A small parking lamp on a car, a required fitting on the vehicle.

clue.text: Sounding futile, but part of a vital system

indicators.note: Sounding means the futile word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a vain effort is a futile one

explanation.surface: Something sounds pointless yet belongs to an essential system.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood vessel carrying blood back to the heart, part of the circulatory system that keeps us alive.

clue.text: Exercise: a modicum that bores

parts.note: a drill is an exercise or practice routine
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: A dull exercise routine, just a little of which is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bores' suggests tedium, but here means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting tool fitted to a drill is the thing that makes holes, boring into material.

clue.text: Killer question: sex appeal before love? Not quite

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the love word

parts.note: how is a question word
it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: Not quite says the last letter of the love word is lost

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A murder-mystery puzzle: does sex appeal come before love?
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is an artillery gun, a deadly weapon, so a killer in the loose sense.

clue.text: Grass one should put back, and maybe does

indicators.note: put back means the grass word is turned around

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A gardener replacing turf that was dug up, as perhaps anyone does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb but is the plural of doe, female deer; 'maybe' flags them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deer are called does, so they are examples of these animals.

clue.text: Wrongly assume school's neither opening nor closing barrier

indicators.note: neither opening nor closing says the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly assumes a school's gate is neither open nor shut.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a famous English boarding school near London; losing its ends leaves ARRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or take on something without right, to assume it wrongfully.

clue.text: Personal attire is reborn?

parts.note: something reborn ..., and personal attire is underwear, so the word splits into un plus dies

explanation.surface: A question whether one's clothing has come back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as UN-DIES, the word means stops being dead, which is what something reborn does.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is informally called this, intimate clothing worn next to the skin.

clue.text: Keep changing opinion — possible cause of schism?

definitions.meaning: to swing back and forth between views
a plank pivoted in the middle which splits two riders up and down

explanation.surface: Flip-flopping views might split a group.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to waver; as a noun it is a playground plank that keeps its riders apart and at odds.

clue.text: Treat an allergy of the vocal organ

indicators.note: Treat signals the letters are processed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Medical advice to treat an allergy affecting the voice box.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relating to the voice box, the throat organ housing the vocal cords.

clue.text: Stop following popular music that's not mainstream

indicators.note: following puts the stop word after the popular word

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
to die is to stop, as an engine does

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to stop following chart music and listen to something alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternative music from small independent labels, outside the commercial mainstream, goes by this name.

clue.text: Like a knife dug finally into journalists

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the journalists

parts.note: ED is short for editor, and two of them stand for journalists

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of dug

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a knife being driven into a group of reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife has a sharp cutting rim, so it is bladed or sharp-sided, a descriptive fit.

clue.text: Fault having backfired, ditches stuff

indicators.note: having backfired means the fault word runs backwards

parts.note: a bug is a fault in software or a machine
to bin something is to throw it away, ditch it

explanation.surface: A faulty engine backfires and ends up in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: GUBBINS is British slang for odds and ends or assorted bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for miscellaneous things or paraphernalia, assorted stuff.

clue.text: Two characters at the rear, one intercepting bribe, very excited

indicators.note: intercepting means the pieces cut into the bribe

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
two zeds are characters at the back end of the alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at catching a bribe being passed at the back of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is British slang for a bribe; the last two letters of the alphabet are ZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of eager energy, as if humming with excitement, is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: In turn, put in answer "trousers"? Yes!

definitions.text: In turn, put in answer "trousers"? Yes!

indicators.note: In turn signals the run is read backwards
put in means the letters sit inside the words answer and trousers

explanation.surface: A quizmaster confirms that the answer is trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'answer' and the start of 'trousers', read backwards; the result is itself a kind of trousers, hence 'Yes!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers, traditionally worn by Scottish regiments.

clue.text: Draw these out to show turning point

indicators.note: out signals the letters are drawn out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to illustrate some turning point.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a moment marking a decisive change, like a ridge dividing rivers that flow different ways.
